svg.aria-label: What runs where. In PowerShell or Windows Terminal, wsl-spawner.exe draws the screen and reads the keys. In a WSL terminal, wsl-spawner, the Linux build of the same program, draws the screen there and asks the .exe for each answer, as JSON. At sign-in and sign-out, Windows starts wsl-spawnerw.exe, the same program with no window: logon starts the distributions you chose, logoff stops them all. The program asks wsl.exe, which lists, starts and stops distributions and runs its scripts in them as root. Inside each distribution set up: start.sh at each start, a service that keeps it running, its notes in /var/lib/wsl-spawner. It sets the sign-in program as you and, as an administrator, the sign-out hook and its wait in the local Group Policy. It reads the event logs after a start that ended without its time. It runs as you, with no network, and no program of it stays running on Windows; a distribution kept running holds Windows' own waitfor.exe.
